t: Iranian-speaking horse nomads related to the Sarmatians, who dominated the steppe north of the Caucasus from the 1st century CE.
Broken by the Huns around 370, some Alans crossed the Rhine in 406 and went on with the Vandals to Spain and North Africa.
Those who stayed in the Caucasus formed the Kingdom of Alania, and the Ossetians speak a language descended from theirs.
dyk: Ammianus Marcellinus wrote that the Alans worshipped a naked sword thrust into the ground as their god of war, and foretold the future with willow rods.
ev: Alans cross the Caucasus and raid Media and Armenia
Arrian, governor of Cappadocia, prepares Roman forces against an Alan invasion
The Huns defeat the Alans near the Don
Alans cross the Rhine with the Vandals and Suebi
The Visigoths destroy the Alans of Hispania and kill their king Addac
Alans cross with the Vandals to North Africa
Alans under Sangiban fight Attila at the Catalaunian Plains
Sarosius helps the first Avar envoys reach Constantinople
